## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 80, titled *Chandaṁadatvāgamana* ("Leaving without giving consent"), is a monastic disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating communal proceedings of the Buddhist monastic Order [SuttaCentral]. The text establishes that if a monk departs from a formal Saṅgha gathering while the community is deliberating an ecclesiastical matter, without having first given his consent (*chanda*), he incurs an offense that must be confessed (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations of the rule and its accompanying commentary include an English version by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The rule has wide parallels across Vinaya literature [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, it corresponds to rule 80 of the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha, is treated in the Bhikkhu Parivāra (Pācittiya 80), and corresponds to Pācittiya 158 of the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and its associated Parivāra and Pātimokkha sections [SuttaCentral]. Parallels exist across multiple early Buddhist traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas [SuttaCentral]. According to DharmaNexus machine alignments, the text shares 324 matching passages with 75 other Pali texts, exhibiting its longest passages of reuse with the Vinaya commentary *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* (§§2.1.10–2.2.3) as well as legal and procedural formulaic segments found throughout the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, including Pācittiya 21, Saṅghādisesa 10, Pācittiya 67, and Pācittiya 46 [DharmaNexus].
